issues.legal_issue: A trust remains within the scope of the provision governing public charitable or religious trusts when it provides benefits to the founder’s family as well as devoting a substantial portion of its income to public charitable or religious purposes.
material_facts: The deed dedicated the property to religious purposes, maintenance of the settlor’s relations and descendants, and the poor and meritorious.
The deed required an annual sum to be spent on mosques and religious schools and on helping the poor and needy, and provided for further charitable contributions if funds permitted.
The deed also provided for the maintenance of the settlor’s family and descendants.
issues.conclusion: The trust was created substantially for a public charitable or religious purpose and fell within the scope of section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure, notwithstanding its provisions benefiting the settlor’s family.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure, whether a trust falls within its scope depends on whether it was created substantially for a public charitable or religious purpose. Family benefits do not take a trust outside the section where a substantial portion of its income is devoted to public charitable or religious purposes. The Court relied on S. Massirat Hossain v. Hossain Ahmad Chowdhury and Vaidya Nath Aiyyar v. Swaminatha Ayyar.

predicates.trust_created_by_dedication: A settlor permanently dedicated property to be held and administered as a trust.
predicates.substantial_income_for_public_charity_or: The trust deed directed a substantial portion of the trust income to public charitable or religious purposes.
predicates.family_benefits_also_provided: The trust deed also provided benefits for the settlor’s family or descendants.

issues.definition: When a trust is created by dedication, devotes a substantial portion of its income to public charitable or religious purposes, and also benefits the settlor’s family, it is created substantially for a public charitable or religious purpose.

issues.legal_issue: A suit seeking the removal and replacement of a trustee of a public charitable or religious trust is subject to the requirement of written consent when it is brought representatively for the trust’s beneficiaries rather than to vindicate a plaintiff’s private right.
material_facts: The suit concerned a trust created substantially for public charitable or religious purposes.
The plaintiff sought a declaration that the trustee was unfit, his removal, the appointment of a replacement trustee, and the appointment of a receiver until the proposed replacement came of age.
The reliefs sought were for the administration of the trust and were not to enforce a private right of the plaintiff.
The suit was treated as brought in a representative capacity on behalf of all the trust’s beneficiaries.
The plaintiff had not obtained the written consent of the Advocate-General.
issues.conclusion: The suit fell within section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure and was not maintainable without the Advocate-General’s written consent.
issues.legal_principle: Section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure applies where a suit concerns a public charitable or religious trust, alleges a breach of trust or seeks directions for its administration, and claims reliefs specified in the section. Even where those conditions are met, the suit must be representative and brought in the public interest, not merely to vindicate an individual or personal right. The Court relied on Budreedas v. Choonilal, Appanna v. Narasinga, and The Tirumalai-Tirupati Devasthanams Committee v. Udiavar Krishnayya Shanbhaga.

rule.if: suit_concerning_public_charitable_or_religious_trust and administration_or_breach_issue and trustee_removal_or_replacement_sought and representative_beneficiary_interest and not written_consent_obtained

predicates.suit_concerning_public_charitable_or_rel: The plaintiff brought a suit concerning a trust created substantially for public charitable or religious purposes.
predicates.administration_or_breach_issue: The suit alleged a breach of trust or sought directions for administering the trust.
predicates.trustee_removal_or_replacement_sought: The plaintiff sought removal of a trustee or appointment of a replacement trustee.
predicates.representative_beneficiary_interest: The plaintiff brought the suit on behalf of the trust’s beneficiaries to protect their common interest, rather than solely to enforce a personal right.
predicates.written_consent_obtained: The plaintiff obtained the Advocate-General’s written consent before bringing the suit.

issues.definition: A suit concerning the administration or alleged breach of a public charitable or religious trust, seeking trustee removal or replacement in the beneficiaries’ representative interest, is not maintainable without the required consent if that consent was not obtained.
